solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wife, imprisoned, absorbing English chiller

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: something absorbing another thing takes it inside itself, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the cooler is slang for prison, so someone imprisoned is in the cooler
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A wife locked away is drinking something cold that came from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imprisoned' looks like a container signal but supplies a two-word phrase; the cooler is slang for a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine cooler is a bucket or appliance that keeps bottles cold, so it is a chiller in the literal sense.

clue.text: Savage pekinese's tail giving a wag

parts.note: savage means wild

indicators.note: a tail is the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of pekinese

explanation.surface: A fierce little dog wags its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Wag is the noun for a witty joker, not a tail movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the famous Irish wit, and a wag is a joker or wit.

clue.text: Spooner's bird of prey sleeps and drinks

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: a kite is a bird of prey and naps are sleeps; swapping their opening sounds gives the answer

explanation.surface: The reverend's hawk dozes and then has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightcaps are drinks taken just before bed.

clue.text: Catholic initially rude about wound getting extreme unction?

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word, so its first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Catholic
to wound is to harm
rude words are offensive

explanation.surface: A Catholic rite, extreme unction, is described in crude terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Extreme unction is the last rites, but here it means extreme unctuousness, oily flattery. 'Rude about wound' places the rude piece after the wound piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm offensive is a campaign of flattery and ingratiation, an extreme dose of unctuousness.

clue.text: Container from India with antique, funny covering

indicators.note: covering something puts it underneath, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: antique means old
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rum is British slang for strange or funny

explanation.surface: A box from India comes with an amusing old cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil drum is a large metal barrel, a container for oil.

clue.text: Clay to win boxing extremely tough European

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing in a box, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: to earn is to win or gain

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes of a word, so its two end letters are kept

parts.note: the outer letters of tough
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A boxer like Cassius Clay beats a hard European opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius Clay was Muhammad Ali's birth name; here clay is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen describes things made of baked clay, so it can replace clay used as an adjective, as in a clay pot.

clue.text: Design information a little bit brief

indicators.note: a brief version of a word is cut short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a speck is a tiny particle

explanation.surface: A designer complains that the details provided are a bit thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spec is short for specification, the detailed technical description a design is built to.

clue.text: Reason waiter might be unhappy, spinning metal spike

indicators.note: spinning turns something round, so the letters are read the other way

parts.note: a waiter who gets no tip is unhappy

explanation.surface: A waiter is upset when a metal skewer goes spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal peg climbers hammer into rock, a spike for securing ropes.

clue.text: Small hole in kind of pink material

indicators.note: in places the preceding word within the following one

parts.note: coral is a pinkish shade
a pore is a tiny opening

explanation.surface: A tiny hole appears in some pink fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Material looks like fabric; it is the adjective meaning physical.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily, of the physical world, which is one sense of material.

clue.text: None too bright Republican splitting party in half?

parts.note: a simple person is not very clever

indicators.note: splitting something means getting between its parts, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a faction is a party or group within a group
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A dim Republican divides his party down the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows half is an example: one half is a simple fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple fraction has whole numbers above and below the line, and one over two is a textbook case.

clue.text: With trouble, hauls item on board a ship

parts.note: to lug is to haul something heavy
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A sailor struggles to drag some piece of gear aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'hauls with trouble', so the trouble piece follows the hauls piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A lugsail is a four-cornered sail hung from a yard, part of a boat's rig.

clue.text: Tories unfortunately meeting resistance in party

indicators.note: something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are put in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Conservatives run into opposition at a political gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is a verb here, not the noun the Tories suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, which is to party in the verb sense.

clue.text: New tech promo, one not carrying a lot of weight

definitions.text: one not carrying a lot of weight

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters are formed afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh advert for gadgets is dismissed as lightweight and unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not carrying a lot of weight' suggests someone without influence, but it is meant physically.
explanation.definitionFit: An ectomorph is a person with a slender, lean build, the body type that carries little fat or muscle.

clue.text: Show article? Keep reading around it

indicators.note: around it means the instruction wraps itself about the item just named, enclosing it

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to carry on to the next page
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a show is worth writing about and is told to read on.
explanation.walkthrough: PTO is printed at the foot of a page to tell the reader to turn over.
explanation.definitionFit: Panto is short for pantomime, the British Christmas stage show for families.

clue.text: Where you might read notes for personnel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the five-line stave on which music is written
second meaning: the employees of an organisation

explanation.surface: A noticeboard where the workforce can read memos.
explanation.walkthrough: The notes look like office memos; they are musical notes on a stave.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical stave is also called a staff, and the staff of a firm are its employees.

clue.text: Often sitting PM's hosted by celebrity Yankee

indicators.note: a guest hosted by someone is taken in by them, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
Anthony Eden was a British Prime Minister
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister spends a lot of time sitting as a guest of a famous American.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. Eden was the British Prime Minister of 1955 to 1957.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes a life or job spent mostly seated.

clue.text: 24 down work after chief lets one go

indicators.note: letting one go means releasing a single I, the roman numeral for one, from the word
after says the first-read piece is placed behind the second one

parts.note: main means chief or principal
an oeuvre is a work, or body of work, of an artist

explanation.surface: A boss sacks someone and the work falls to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 down is DODGE, a cross-reference standing in for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A manoeuvre is an evasive move, the same as a dodge.

clue.text: Vetting odd article in Le Figaro? You'll have a hand in this

definitions.text: You'll have a hand in this

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are arranged in a strange new way

parts.note: taken as written
un is the French indefinite article, the sort found in a French paper

explanation.surface: Checking a strange piece in a Paris newspaper is a task you'll share in.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Figaro is a French daily paper; the French setting also hints at the game's French name.
explanation.definitionFit: Vingt-et-un is the card game also called pontoon or blackjack, so a player has a hand in it.

clue.text: Hide unfinished design on copper vessel

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter goes
in an across clue, on means placed after, so the design piece follows

parts.note: DI, a Detective Inspector, is a police officer, and copper is slang for one
SS stands for steamship
an emblem is a design used as a symbol

explanation.surface: A half-made pattern is stamped on a pot made of copper.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like the metal of the vessel; it is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissemble is to disguise one's true feelings, so to hide them.

clue.text: One seen in parties or bar, but sloshed around noon

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, and a drunk's words come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted at parties or in a pub, drunk by midday.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a lucky dip, a tub of bran with prizes hidden in it, a staple of British children's parties and fetes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bran tub is a party game, so it is something one sees at children's parties.

clue.text: Final Deutschmark in French and East German banks

indicators.note: banks line either side of a river, so two pieces flank another

parts.note: en is French for in
DM is the abbreviation for the Deutschmark
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: The last Deutschmark is deposited in French and East German banks.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks looks financial alongside the Deutschmark; it means the two sides that flank the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means furthest towards the end, so final.

clue.text: Free of hesitation, fantastic learner of the organ

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful and unreal, so the letters take a fanciful new order
the hesitation sound er is the thing to be freed from, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An organist's star pupil plays without faltering.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the conventional hesitation; taking it from the learner leaves five letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the adjective relating to the kidneys, the organ in question.

clue.text: Posterior part of human, possibly seat?

definitions.text: Posterior part of human, possibly seat?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible arrangement among several, so the letters may be reordered
the posterior part of a word is its rear, so its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of human
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a seat might be described as the back end of a person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while also giving the wordplay: the rear letter of human plus a rearranged seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nates is the anatomical Latin word for the buttocks, the part of the body one sits on.

clue.text: Part of e.g. Holly's swimwear, but not all of it

indicators.note: not all of a word means some of it is cut, here the final letter

parts.note: swimming trunks are men's swimwear

explanation.surface: Holly's swimsuit is skimpy, covering only part of her.
explanation.walkthrough: Holly looks like a woman's name, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the main stem of a tree such as holly.

clue.text: Jack stopped working, collaring e.g. Tom for what Edward did

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation

indicators.note: collaring someone means seizing them round the neck, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a machine that has stopped working has died
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A man downs tools and grabs someone, explaining Edward's conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward VIII gave up the British throne in 1936 to marry Wallis Simpson.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward VIII renounced the crown, which is what abdicating means.

clue.text: Avoid meeting magistrate around 1st of December

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece goes about another

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
the first letter of December

explanation.surface: Someone tries to escape an encounter with a judge at the start of December.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to evade it, so dodge and avoid are synonyms.

clue.text: Spirit, as in Bible, with appealing quality

indicators.note: in places the preceding word inside the following one

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
qua is a Latin-derived word meaning as or in the capacity of
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A spiritual text is praised as having real charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit looks religious beside the Bible, but it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquavit is a Scandinavian spirit distilled from grain or potatoes and flavoured with caraway.

clue.text: Hand in reference work that's neglected

indicators.note: in places the preceding word within the following one

parts.note: the OED, Oxford English Dictionary, is the classic reference work
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Someone submits a reference book that has been ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand in' reads as a phrasal verb meaning submit, but hand is the piece and in is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omitted has been left out, which is to say neglected.

clue.text: Picked up yellow tie

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, as a radio picks up a signal

parts.note: the yolk is the yellow part of an egg

explanation.surface: Someone collects a yellow necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoke is a bond that couples two things together, as it links a pair of oxen.

clue.text: Laying off flipping idiot during time off

indicators.note: during means within a span, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: absence is time away from work

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round end to end

parts.note: a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: Workers are being laid off by an idiot boss while staff are on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swearword qualifying idiot; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is refraining from something such as drink, so laying off it.
